report: Resident A had a low appetite today but managed to eat half of her breakfast with some encouragement; she needed full assistance with lunch, showing signs of choking twice despite using an adapted cup. Hydration levels are on track.

Resident B displayed increased restlessness throughout the night and wandered the hall twice. Staff helped her back to bed and noted she slept fitfully. She complained of back pain but rested more comfortably after medication was administered.

Resident C enjoyed a brief visit from her family, which seemed to lift her spirits. Afterwards, she participated in a short organized activity involving browsing through a magazine but showed apathy soon after. Her nails were trimmed today.

Resident D experienced tightness of breath and reported nausea after lunch. Medication was administered as per the care plan, with frequent checks throughout the day to ensure comfort. Minor medical concerns will be discussed with the family and GP during the care meeting.

Resident E displayed subtle signs of confusion and needed continual reminders to use his walking aid. There was one fall incident but no apparent injuries. Assistance was needed for transfers and lifts throughout the day due to increased agitation.

Mrs. Thompson had a peaceful night. She slept well, without any significant restlessness or episodes of confusion. She required assistance with dressing and grooming this morning. However, she complained quietly about a persistent back pain, and caregivers provided support to manage her discomfort. There was no noted agitation during the day. Nutrition intake was positive, though she needed encouragement to eat her breakfast.

Mr. Johnson showed signs of increased oedema in his lower extremities today, which required additional care and monitoring. He managed to eat a small portion of his meals with adapted cutlery but needed ample encouragement. A brief family visit seemed to lift his spirits, though he mostly observed quietly. Care staff noted minor redness on his skin but no major pressure ulcers. Despite some apathy, he was engaged briefly by flipping through a magazine.

Today, Mrs. Lee was mildly confused, occasionally forgetting where she was. She did not express severe discomfort but reported intermittent nausea and needed assistance with toileting several times throughout the night. Her daughter visited her in the afternoon, which seemed to calm her considerably. Hydration was monitored carefully due to her tendency to drink less. No major medical issues were communicated, but ongoing palliative support was discussed with her family.

Mr. Alvarez had difficulty with restlessness overnight, wandering the halls and requiring gentle redirection back to his room. He showed some signs of apathy throughout the day and expressed a feeling of tightness in his chest, which was managed promptly by the staff. His nutritional intake remains a concern, as he only managed small sips of liquids despite regular encouragement. Minor skin redness was noted during the morning routine.

Ms. Green required full assistance with her morning routine, including brushing her teeth and getting dressed. She was somewhat agitated, expressing subtle pain in her joints but was comforted by the care team. During a routine skin check, a slight pressure ulcer was observed and treated immediately. A staff member spent time with her engaged in light conversation, which seemed to ease her apathy somewhat. Her afternoon was calmer after she received her prescribed medication.

The resident had a restless night, showing frequent signs of agitation and confusion. They frequently called out for assistance and were found lying crookedly in bed several times. Medication was administered as per their care plan to alleviate discomfort, but minimal relief was noted.

Today, the resident needed full assistance with dressing and brushing their teeth. They were given a sponge bath and their dental prostheses were cleaned. Despite offering their favorite meal, they consumed only a few bites and showed signs of nausea throughout the day. Encouragement was provided to maintain hydration.

The resident participated in a small, organized group activity this afternoon, browsing through a magazine with the help of staff. They received visitors during this time, but remained largely unresponsive and apathetic. Encouragement for social interaction yielded minimal engagement.

Assessment revealed increased oedema and redness on the resident's legs. Their toenails were also noted to be too long, requiring attention. A new care plan discussion was initiated to address these skin conditions and ensure their comfort.

Despite several attempts to calm them, the resident displayed signs of pain and restlessness today. Assistance was required for transfers to and from the wheelchair due to their weakened state. A family request was put in for a reassessment of their pain management protocol to improve their quality of life in these palliative stages.

Resident A was assisted with showering and dressing this morning. They required full assistance due to limited mobility but were cooperative throughout the process. During breakfast, Resident A was encouraged to eat but only consumed a small portion of porridge; nutrition intake is being closely monitored. Noteworthy was an increase in restlessness and mild agitation noted during the day, requiring additional comfort and reassurance. Observed some redness and peeling on the heels, care cream applied as per protocol. Resident A also reported mild back pain, pain relief medication was administered as prescribed.

Resident B was attended to for hygiene care, including getting ready for the day, brushing their teeth, and morning dressing. They needed complete support. At lunch, Resident B used adapted cutlery and ate most of their meal but required prompts to drink water. No visitors today, but the resident enjoyed looking through a magazine briefly in the afternoon. There were signs of nail overgrowth; a request for a private podiatrist visit has been made. Resident B seemed confused at multiple points during the day, although orientation interventions were applied. Complaints of nausea were reported; palliative care team informed and antiemetic provided as necessary.

Resident C experienced restlessness several times during the night, requiring assistance with re-positioning and making phone calls. Morning rounds noted some slight oedema in the ankles, continuing to monitor. During the day, Resident C had minimal engagement in organised activities, displaying apathy and a lack of interest. Lunch consisted of mashed potatoes and vegetables which Resident C consumed independently. However, hydration remains a concern, and supplemental drinks are being encouraged. Residents had a minor episode of tightness of breath mid-afternoon; oxygen levels were checked, and oxygen therapy was administered as per care plan.

In the morning, Resident D received assistance with dressing, washing up, and cleaning dental prostheses. In terms of eating, Resident D needed some encouragement and used a specialised cup to stay hydrated. There was noted anxiety before lunchtime, necessitating calm assurance and support. During the afternoon, Resident D interacted briefly with fellow residents. Notable blotching and redness were observed on the arms, ideal for monitoring skin conditions and treatment adjustments. Minor soreness was reported, requiring short-term pain management which the resident responded well to.

Resident E was given help with evening shower and dressing, needing full aid as they are largely bed-bound. Dinner included several soft foods, primarily soup, which the resident accepted when given full feeding assistance. Swallowing difficulties and risk of choking observed; hence increased supervision during meal times implemented. Evening rounds recorded instances of resident confusion and mild agitation. An incident of soiling after incontinence was efficiently and empathetically handled. A caregiver noted discomfort registering as mild abdominal pain; prompt assessment was carried out with continued observation advised.
